examples.en: On the snowy road, I walked carefully with every step.

examples.ko: 고향 거리를 걸으니 걸음걸음마다 추억이 떠올라요.
examples.en: Walking the streets of my hometown, memories come to mind at every step.
The pilgrim walked the road praying with every step.

examples.ko: 어머니는 걸음걸음 아이를 걱정하며 집으로 돌아가셨어요.
examples.en: My mother went home worrying about her child with every step.

examples.ko: 산길은 걸음걸음 땀이 날 만큼 가팔랐어요.
examples.en: The mountain path was so steep that every step made me sweat.

examples.ko: 이 길은 걸음걸음 새로운 풍경이 펼쳐져요.
examples.en: On this path, a new view opens up with every step.

explain: 한 걸음 한 걸음마다라는 느낌으로, '걸음걸음마다' 형태로도 자주 써요. 말할 때보다 글이나 감성적인 표현에서 어울려요. 걷는 모양을 뜻하는 '걸음걸이'와 헷갈리지 마세요.
explain_en: It carries the feel of 'at each and every step' and is also used in the form '걸음걸음마다'. It suits writing and emotional expression more than casual talk. Don't confuse it with '걸음걸이', which means the way someone walks.

examples.ko: 작년 여름에 제주도에 갔어요. 고맘때 날씨가 정말 좋았어요.
examples.en: I went to Jeju Island last summer. The weather around that time was really nice.
Kids are the cutest right around that age.
Around that age, everyone goes through puberty.
I thought like that at that age too.
I still remember the snacks I ate around that time.

examples.ko: 친구는 작년 가을에 취직했어요. 저도 고맘때에는 꼭 취직하고 싶어요.
examples.en: My friend got a job last fall. I really want to have a job by around that time too.

explain: 지나간 때나 나이를 가리키며 '그맘때'가 더 흔해요. '고맘때'는 같은 뜻으로 쓰지만 조금 더 가볍고 귀엽게 들려요. 가까운 때를 말하는 '이맘때'와 짝으로 기억하세요.
explain_en: It points to a time or age already mentioned, and '그맘때' is more common. '고맘때' has the same meaning but sounds a little lighter and cuter. Remember it as a pair with '이맘때' (around this time).

examples.en: It's already in the past, so let's forget it as bygones.
That matter is all in the past now.
If you cling to the past, it's hard to move forward.

examples.ko: 둘이 싸운 건 과거지사니까 이제 화해해요.
examples.en: The fight between you two is in the past, so make up now.
Don't keep bringing up the past.
Even hard times become things of the past once they're over.

explain: 이미 지나간 일이라 더 따지지 않겠다는 마음을 담아서 '과거지사로 하다/치다', '다 과거지사예요'처럼 말해요. 그냥 '과거'는 시간을 말하고, '과거지사'는 지난 일을 이제는 문제 삼지 않는 분위기가 있어요. 화해하거나 위로할 때 자주 써요.
explain_en: It carries the feeling of not dwelling on something already over, as in '과거지사로 하다/치다' or '다 과거지사예요'. Plain '과거' just refers to time, while '과거지사' has a tone of no longer making an issue of what has passed. It is often used when making up with someone or comforting them.

examples.en: It was last December. Around that time it snowed a lot.
Kids of that age love toys.
I was very short at that age too.
Around that time, flowers start to bloom.
Next March? By around then I'll have graduated too.
It was around that very time that I met my friend.

explain: 앞에서 말한 때나 나이 무렵을 가리켜요. 지금 이 무렵은 '이맘때'라고 하고, 같은 짝으로 '저맘때'도 있어요. '작년 이맘때'처럼 시기를 말할 때 자주 써요.
explain_en: It points to the time or age mentioned earlier. For the present time of year, use '이맘때', and there is also '저맘때' in the same set. It's often used for periods, as in '작년 이맘때'.

en: in the meantime; already, by now

examples.en: The rain has already stopped in the meantime.

examples.ko: 잠깐 자리를 비운 그새에 누가 가방을 가져갔어요.
examples.en: Someone took my bag in the short time I was away.

examples.ko: 오랜만에 봤더니 그새 키가 많이 컸어요.
examples.en: I haven't seen you in a while, and you've grown so much already.

examples.ko: 밥 먹고 왔는데 그새 줄이 길어졌어요.
examples.en: I came back from eating and the line had already gotten long.

examples.ko: 엄마가 잠깐 나간 그새 동생이 과자를 다 먹었어요.
examples.en: In the short while Mom was out, my little brother ate all the snacks.

examples.ko: 며칠 안 본 그새 얼굴이 좋아졌네요.
examples.en: In just the few days I didn't see you, your face has improved.

explain: '그새'는 '그사이'를 줄인 말로 짧은 시간 안에 일이 달라졌을 때 써요. 놀라움이나 아쉬움이 같이 들어 있어요. '그동안'은 긴 시간에도 쓰지만 '그새'는 짧은 시간의 변화에 더 어울려요.
explain_en: 그새 is a short form of 그사이 and is used when something changes within a short time. It carries a feeling of surprise or regret. 그동안 can cover a long period, but 그새 fits a change over a short time better.

en: a little longer than a month; about a month

examples.en: It has been a little over a month since I moved.
I met that friend about a month ago.
The trip seems like it will take about a month.
I was in the hospital for as long as a month.

examples.ko: 아기가 태어난 지 달포밖에 안 됐어요.
examples.en: The baby has been born for only about a month.
The construction finished in about a month.

explain: 딱 한 달이 아니라 '한 달 남짓'이라는 느낌이라서 '달포쯤', '달포 만에'처럼 써요. 앞에 숫자를 붙이지 않아요. 일상 대화에서는 '한 달 정도'라고 많이 말하고, 달포는 글이나 어르신 말투에서 들을 수 있어요.
explain_en: It means a little over a month rather than exactly one, and is used as '달포쯤' or '달포 만에'. You do not put a number in front of it. In daily talk people often say '한 달 정도', and 달포 is heard in writing or from older speakers.

examples.ko: 만추의 단풍이 산 전체를 붉게 물들였어요.
examples.en: The late-autumn leaves painted the whole mountain red.
Now that it's late autumn, the streets are full of fallen leaves.
I planned a train trip to take in late autumn.

examples.ko: 이 영화는 만추를 배경으로 한 사랑 이야기예요.
examples.en: This movie is a love story set in late autumn.
Early November is a time you can call late autumn.

examples.ko: 깊어 가는 만추라서 저녁 공기가 쌀쌀해요.
examples.en: It's deep into late autumn, so the evening air is chilly.

explain: 늦가을을 가리키는 글 느낌의 말이에요. 말할 때는 '늦가을'이 훨씬 자연스럽고, 만추는 시나 글, 안내문에서 더 많이 보여요. 분위기를 살리고 싶을 때 골라 써요.
explain_en: It refers to late autumn and has a written, literary feel. In speech '늦가을' is much more natural, while 만추 appears more in poems, essays and notices. Choose it when you want to set a mood.

examples.en: My grandfather farmed while he was alive.
I want to be good to my parents while they are alive.
It's a song my father loved to sing while he was alive.

examples.ko: 살아생전에 한 번이라도 더 찾아뵐걸 그랬어요.
examples.en: I wish I had visited him one more time while he was alive.
That person helped many people during their lifetime.

examples.ko: 살아생전의 모습이 사진 속에 그대로 남아 있어요.
examples.en: The way they looked in life remains just the same in the photo.

explain: 주로 돌아가신 분을 떠올리며 '그분이 살아 계실 때'라는 느낌으로 말해요. '생전에'로 줄여 말하기도 해요. 자기 부모님이나 자신에 대해 '살아 있는 동안'의 뜻으로 쓸 수도 있어요.
explain_en: It is mostly used when remembering someone who has passed away, with the feel of 'when they were alive'. People also shorten it to '생전에'. It can also refer to your own parents or yourself in the sense of 'while one is alive'.

examples.en: I spent my childhood in the countryside.

examples.ko: 그 노래를 들으면 유년의 기억이 떠올라요.
examples.en: When I hear that song, memories of my childhood come back.
Habits learned in early childhood last a long time.
The writer said he spent his childhood in poverty.

examples.ko: 우리 할머니는 유년 이야기를 자주 해 주세요.
examples.en: My grandmother often tells me stories from her childhood.
For children in early childhood, play is the most important thing.

explain: 보통 '유년 시절', '유년기'처럼 붙여 써요. 일상에서는 '어린 시절'이 자연스럽고, '유년'은 글이나 인터뷰에서 더 문학적으로 들려요. '유아기'는 더 어린 때를 가리켜요.
explain_en: It is usually attached to another word, as in '유년 시절' or '유년기'. In daily talk '어린 시절' is more natural, while '유년' sounds more literary in writing and interviews. '유아기' refers to an even younger age.

examples.en: I took a walk in the neighborhood park at dusk.
When dusk came, the sky turned red.
I was on my way home around dusk.

examples.ko: 시골에서는 해거름이면 저녁 짓는 냄새가 났어요.
examples.en: In the countryside, the smell of dinner cooking drifted by at dusk.
The beach at dusk was truly beautiful.
We worked in the field until dusk.

explain: 해가 지기 시작하는 무렵을 말하는데, '저녁'보다 글 같고 정서적인 느낌이 있어요. 같은 때를 '해 질 녘'이라고도 해요. 소설이나 시골 풍경을 이야기할 때 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: It refers to the time when the sun begins to set, and feels more literary and sentimental than '저녁' (evening). The same time is also called '해 질 녘'. It suits novels and descriptions of countryside scenery.
